messages.author: ea4c852d208ad39b
messages.subject: making own geom
parts:
Hi Hadley, ggplot2 users and addicts,

I am a big fan of ggplot2 but sometimes I want to plot 'special graphs that are not supported. Supposing that I want to build my own geom, how do I do that? and where do I start?

Cheers,

Julius

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: making own geom
parts:
Hi Julius,

Two suggestions:

1) Read the attached draft of a chapter on writing your own objects
that never made it into the book. It's very very rough, but will
hopefully give you some pointers.

2) Read the source code for some of the simpler geoms like
geom_point, geom_rect and geom_text. Then have a look at more
complicated ones like geom_line and geom_boxplot. When you're starting
off, you can ignore all the coordinate transformation stuff - that
only matters if you want your geom to work in non-Cartesian coordinate
systems.

Hadley
